config.title: Infinite Scroll

intro.title: Infinite Scroll
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that implements an infinite scroll feature, allowing users to load more content automatically as they scroll down a list. You will learn the core concept of detecting scroll events and conditionally triggering data fetches to simulate loading additional items. The main technologies involved include Angular's built-in directives, event handling, and TypeScript for managing state and logic. By the end, you'll have a working component that dynamically adds new items to a list, providing a seamless user experience common in modern web apps.
intro.usecase: Infinite scroll is a fundamental pattern in modern web applications where content loads continuously as users scroll down, eliminating the need for pagination buttons. You'll find this implemented in social media feeds like Facebook and Twitter, e-commerce product listings on Amazon, and content platforms like YouTube's video suggestions. As an Angular developer, you'll use infinite scroll to build data-heavy dashboards, news aggregators, or any interface where users browse through large datasets seamlessly. This pattern improves user experience by reducing initial load times while keeping engagement high through smooth, uninterrupted browsing.

objectives: Initialize a component with state to manage a dynamic list of items and a loading flag.
Implement a service method to fetch paginated data from an API.
Configure an event handler to detect when the user scrolls near the bottom of the page.
Integrate the scroll event handler with the data fetching service to load more items.
Update the component's template to bind and display the growing list of items.
Control the visibility of a loading indicator based on the component's state.
Apply Angular lifecycle hooks to set up and clean up scroll event listeners.

steps.instruction: In the app.module.ts file, import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and import HttpClientModule from '@angular/common/http'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement syntax: import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core'; and import { HttpClientModule } from '@angular/common/http';

steps.title: Create the main component class
steps.instruction: Create a new component class named InfiniteScrollComponent that implements OnInit.
steps.hint: Define a class with the correct name and implements keyword, then add the ngOnInit method.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named InfiniteScrollComponent is created with the OnInit interface implemented.
successCriteria: The code contains a class named InfiniteScrollComponent that implements OnInit and has a ngOnInit method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your class is named InfiniteScrollComponent and implements OnInit with a ngOnInit method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a class with the exact name InfiniteScrollComponent that implements OnInit.

steps.title: Initialize component state variables
steps.instruction: Inside the InfiniteScrollComponent class, declare four class properties: items as an empty array of any type, currentPage as a number initialized to 1, isLoading as a boolean initialized to false, and hasMore as a boolean initialized to true.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript type annotations for each property. For example: items: any[] = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class will have four typed properties to manage scroll data and loading state.
successCriteria: The InfiniteScrollComponent class contains items (any[]), currentPage (number), isLoading (boolean), and hasMore (boolean) properties with correct initial values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've declared some properties, but check if all four (items, currentPage, isLoading, hasMore) are present with correct types and initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is missing required state variables. Make sure to declare items (array), currentPage (number), isLoading (boolean), and hasMore (boolean) as class properties.

steps.title: Inject HttpClient service
steps.instruction: In the InfiniteScrollComponent constructor, inject the HttpClient service as a private parameter named 'http'.
steps.hint: Use Angular's dependency injection by adding a constructor parameter with type HttpClient and the private access modifier.

constructor(private dataService: DataService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The HttpClient service will be available throughout the component via the 'http' property for making API calls.
successCriteria: HttpClient is injected as a private parameter named 'http' in the constructor.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the HttpClient parameter has the 'private' modifier and is named 'http'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HttpClient service needs to be injected as a constructor parameter. Try adding 'private http: HttpClient' inside the constructor parentheses.

steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnInit method, call the loadItems method to fetch initial data when the component initializes.
steps.hint: Angular calls ngOnInit after creating the component. Add a call to this.loadItems() inside the ngOnInit method body.

successCriteria: ngOnInit contains a call to this.loadItems()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling this.loadItems() inside the ngOnInit method body.

steps.instruction: Add the component's template with a main container div and a placeholder for the items list.

steps.title: Display loaded items in template
steps.instruction: In the component template, use the *ngFor directive to iterate through the items array and display each item's content in a list.
steps.hint: Add a <ul> element with an *ngFor directive that loops through 'items' and displays each item in an <li> element.

steps.instruction: Implement the onScroll method in your component that checks if the user has scrolled to the bottom and calls loadItems when more items exist.
